lesson: The octave-low Zyn PAD mismatch came from conflating spectral table root with note playback frequency. `spectrum root` must own table/base frequency, while `freq` owns the played note. evidence: PatchScript now preserves spectrum freq as voice note frequency; PatchScriptTests.SpectralBankSeparatesTableRootFromPlaybackFrequency covers the invariant; artifacts/parity/zyn-pad-reference/report.txt records the improved score.

lesson: Aqua's remaining detuned impression was caused by stacking same-note PAD spectral voices. Collapse body/high content into one coherent spectral table before adding layers for richness. A simple gain trim then brought loudness into line: RMS ratio 1.001704, centroid ratio 1.004072, score 0.6211.
evidence: BuiltInScripts.ZynStylePadTexture now uses one active PAD spectrum with partials 1, 1.5, and 2 plus patch gain 1.1; artifacts/parity/zyn-pad-reference/report.txt records the focused render.

lesson: More PAD fixtures immediately exposed which pressure is real: `pad-pure` and old `pad-texture` render identically through Zyn, so the filter/category XML in `pad-texture` was not live oracle behavior. `pad-harmonic` changes table and note output through explicit OSCIL harmonics and should be the next PAD parity rung.
evidence: tests/AquaSynth.Dsl.Tests/Fixtures/ZynAddSubFX/ProjectAuthored/pad-pure.xiz and pad-harmonic.xiz plus artifacts/parity/zyn-pad-fixtures/report.txt.

lesson: GPL Zyn presets are acceptable as test-only feedstock. The upstream instrument submodule at `external/zynaddsubfx/instruments` commit c5c912131b31df5fdf372d2f06a25aaf2375837f provides 1318 `.xiz` files; survey and PAD render tests write ignored reports/WAVs while the NuGet boundary still excludes `.xiz`, `external/`, and artifacts.
evidence: ZynInstrumentTests.SurveysUpstreamGplInstrumentBankWhenAvailable and ZynReferenceParityTests.ZynPadReferenceRendererSurveysUpstreamGplPadFixturesWhenBuilt; focused Zyn tests passed 14/14.

lesson: Zyn PAD listening artifacts now follow the DX7 parity shape: per-synth timestamped run folders with Zyn reference WAVs, source-table WAVs, `report.txt`, and `candidate.aqua`. Upstream GPL PAD runs write `candidate-aquasynth.wav`; this was initially the current ZynStylePadTexture baseline and is now superseded by generated per-preset PAD rebuilds.
evidence: ZynReferenceParityTests focused run passed 4/4 and wrote folders such as artifacts/parity/zyn-upstream-pad-fixtures/0121-ghost-ensemble-20260515T072330036.

lesson: Zyn PAD artifacts now use per-preset generated `.aqua` instead of the generic baseline. `ZynInstrumentReader.RebuildFirstPadAsAquaSynthScript` translates the first enabled PAD kit item into one named PAD layer plus a `spectrum` bank using OSCIL harmonic magnitudes, Zyn oracle sample `basefreq` as table root, PAD volume as layer gain, and simple rate/level envelope scaffolding. Reports explicitly list missing Zyn semantics: bandwidth/profile spreading, harmonic profile shaping, and filter envelope/LFO lowering.
evidence: ZynInstrumentTests.RebuildsProjectAuthoredPadAsAquaSynthSpectrumScript plus focused Zyn tests passed 13/13; latest upstream PAD reports include generated candidate scripts and log-mel scores from ~0.276 to ~0.637.

lesson: Zyn PAD bandwidth/profile/position fields belong on SpectralBank as table-generation data, not in parity side channels. Mapping those fields and Zyn's exponential PAD volume curve improved gain/envelope evidence, but profile math alone did not solve log-mel parity.
evidence: Focused Zyn tests passed 13/13 after adding PadSpectrumProfile and zyn_* script fields; upstream PAD batch still has log-mel roughly 0.34-0.69 depending on fixture.

lesson: Expanding a subset of Zyn OscilGen base_function plus spectrum_adjust is conceptually the right owner for one-harmonic PAD presets, but the first approximation is mixed and must not be treated as solved parity.
evidence: Soft Pad log-mel improved to 0.342738 and Organ Choir Pad2 to 0.573216, while sin2x pad regressed to 0.524421, DoublePadBass to 0.689315, and Ghost Ensemble to 0.482155. Next cut needs more OscilGen semantics or gating.

lesson: Zyn OscilGen partial extraction should only run the sampled waveform pipeline when oscillator processing stages are live; otherwise direct harmonics stay readable and capped. A broad base-function expansion made some presets worse without earning its complexity.
evidence: After adding sampled filter/waveshape/modulation stage order and restoring a capped direct path, sin2x pad improved to log-mel 0.455193, while Soft Pad stayed 0.342738 and Ghost stayed 0.40922. DoublePadBass and Organ Choir remain poor, so this is an incremental rung, not parity.

lesson: Do not treat first enabled PAD kit item as a Zyn instrument when kit_mode is multi-kit. Multi-kit PAD presets need per-kit table roots and layered Aqua spectrum banks, or parity artifacts compare against an amputated preset.
evidence: DoublePadBass has kit_mode=1 with enabled PAD kit items 0 and 1. Rebuilding/summing both moved log-mel from about 0.655 to 0.493 and generated doublepadbass_0 plus doublepadbass_1. Raising the volume cap to 3.0 worsened log-mel to 0.521 and was cut.

lesson: A direct-harmonic readability gate must not erase source identity. Ghost Ensemble needed power-base OscilGen expansion even without downstream oscillator stages; otherwise it collapsed toward a generic two-partial pad.
evidence: Ghost Ensemble has base_function=4 with two explicit harmonics. Expanding power-base multi-harmonic sources changed the candidate from two partials to 32 partials and improved score to 0.446977, with log-mel 0.402789.

lesson: Zyn PAD static global filter frequency is audible layer-balance authority, not optional decoration. Read nested FILTER params under FILTER_PARAMETERS and lower old Zyn cutoff values through the exponential FilterParams curve, not a linear freq/127 guess.
evidence: DoublePadBass kit0 filter freq=12 and kit1 freq=61. Linear mapping gave lpf=0.094488/0.480315 and still sounded like all kazoo. Zyn's curve maps them to lpf=0.003325/0.047225, improving log-mel to 0.334546 and making the generated patch deep-bass-first. Filter envelopes/LFOs and level recovery remain missing pressure.

lesson: Zyn PAD note frequency is not just the requested note plus table root; FREQUENCY_PARAMETERS coarse/fine detune are live playback authority, and analog LP2 needs a steeper low-pass than AquaSynth's old one-pole default.
evidence: DoublePadBass has coarse_detune=15360, which Zyn getdetune wraps from octave 15 to -1 octave. Emitting spectrum freq=130.8128 instead of 261.6256 and lpf_order=2 moved DoublePadBass log-mel from 0.334546 after static cutoff mapping to 0.259298; remaining gap is RMS/envelope.

lesson: Zyn PAD FILTER_ENVELOPE is audible transient authority. Static cutoff parity can get the tone right while still missing the opening hit; AquaSynth needs explicit low-pass cutoff envelopes with nonzero start levels.
evidence: DoublePadBass sounded tonally right but softer at onset. Mapping Zyn ADSR-filter octave offsets into lpf_env=rl with lpf_start improved log-mel from 0.259298 to 0.241993, envelope distance from 0.631427 to 0.554658, RMS ratio from 0.390177 to 0.456173, and score from 0.370218 to 0.404382.

lesson: After PAD table roots, detune, filter order, filter envelope, and logarithmic envelope times are mapped, remaining Zyn PAD loudness can be a generated-rebuild output calibration rather than another per-layer fixture tweak.
evidence: Current PAD fixture RMS ratios before calibration were consistently low: DoublePadBass 0.511669, Soft Pad 0.619347, Organ Choir 0.588127, Ghost 0.730155, sin2x 0.775653. Emitting patch gain=1.6 moved DoublePadBass candidate WAV peak to 0.979 against clipped Zyn reference peak 1.0, envelope distance to 0.226563, RMS ratio to 0.818669, and score to 0.631168 while keeping batch RMS plausible.

lesson: Zyn PAD analog filter Q is real filter damping authority and belongs as a general AquaSynth filter surface (`lpf_q`), not as a fixture-specific cutoff/gain fudge.
evidence: Ghost Ensemble has FILTER freq_track=97 and q=28. Adding note-tracked cutoff lowered Ghost lpf from 0.369706 to 0.282776 and adding explicit lpf_q=0.499021 moved log-mel from 0.38424 to 0.375637 and RMS ratio from 1.155288 to 1.09995. DoublePadBass remained acceptable and improved to log-mel 0.247729 / score 0.650069 after Q.

lesson: Explicit low-pass Q must not erase low-pass order. When a reference filter has both damping and slope, Faust lowering should cascade resonant stages according to `lpf_order` rather than replacing the filter with one generic resonant low-pass.
evidence: Ghost Ensemble still sounded bright in the middle after lpf_q. Cascading resonlp stages for lpf_order=4 moved Ghost log-mel from 0.375637 to 0.369402 and RMS ratio from 1.09995 to 1.054875 while keeping DoublePadBass near its accepted score: log-mel 0.247748, score 0.650029. ZynPadReference harmonic dumps showed Ghost's first 32 imported OscilGen partial ratios already matched Zyn, so this was filter slope, not first-page harmonic extraction.

lesson: Zyn OscilGen oscillator filter functions use one-based harmonic indices. Do not translate them through a zero-based AquaSynth index; that moves spectral features to the wrong partial and can make a preset sound like the wrong overtone is being emphasized.
evidence: sin2x uses oscillator filter type 13. With zero-based indexing, AquaSynth put the spike on h3 and had centroid ratio 1.227953. After preserving Zyn's one-based index, candidate partials are h2-dominant, centroid ratio improves to 0.998145, log-mel moves from 0.491437 to 0.479782, and UpstreamSin2xOscilFilterKeepsSpikeOnSecondHarmonicWhenAvailable asserts h2 > h3 * 10.

lesson: Organ Choir's coherent octave blast needs real Zyn PAD high-pass ownership and selected table roots for OscilGen shift-base sources, but selected roots must not become the global default. The source rule is narrow: keep sample-0 roots unless the PAD OscilGen base function is the shift source (`base_function=7`) and the oracle provides the selected note table root.
evidence: Organ Choir kit0 has analog HP2 with stages and FILTER_ENVELOPE, while kit1 uses base_function=7. Mapping hpf_order/hpf_env and using the selected 622.25 Hz table root only for kit1 moved the candidate's dominant peak to 522.67 Hz with 261 Hz at -1.29 dB, close to Zyn's 523.33 Hz lead and 261 Hz at -2.23 dB. Latest Organ log-mel is 0.499122 / score 0.51966, while accepted Soft Pad, Ghost, and DoublePadBass remain on sample-0 roots; global selected roots had regressed DoublePadBass.

lesson: Organ Choir's violin-vs-wind mismatch was OscilGen source-table ownership, not pitch, envelope, or gain. Zyn `base_function_modulation` warps the phase before base-function sampling, and `adaptive_harmonics` remaps the prepared oscillator spectrum at the PAD table root; both must happen before PAD bandwidth/profile spreading.
evidence: Before the fix, Aqua kit1 partials formed a smooth ramp (h3 -3.5 dB, h4 -5.1 dB, h8 -10.2 dB relative to h1) while Zyn's harmonic dump was sparse (h3 -27.1 dB, h4 -70.3 dB, h8 -50.2 dB). Applying base_function_modulation=1 and adaptive_harmonics=1 moved kit1 table energy to 400-800 Hz 0.2713 vs Zyn 0.2780 and 8-16 kHz 0.1471 vs Zyn 0.1355; Organ log-mel improved to 0.471483 and score to 0.541933 without changing accepted DoublePadBass, Ghost, or Soft Pad.

lesson: For sustained Zyn PAD fixtures, log-mel distance can remain pessimistic after the perceptual target has been reached. Keep it as a regression and triage signal, but do not keep grinding accepted fixtures solely to chase a DX7-like numeric threshold when listening and structural source-table evidence agree.
evidence: After mapping selected roots, HP filter motion, Q/order cascades, one-based OscilGen filter indices, base-function phase modulation, and adaptive harmonics, the user accepted DoublePadBass, Ghost Ensemble, Soft Pad, Organ Choir, and the other recent community PAD fixtures by ear. Organ Choir still reports log-mel 0.471483 despite direct kit1 table energy matching the Zyn body/air balance and the listener judging all fixtures equivalent.

lesson: Reference-synth names must not become canonical AquaSynth syntax or public patch-model vocabulary. Importers may translate Zyn controls, and parser aliases may keep old parity artifacts readable, but generated/authored `.aqua` should use AquaSynth-native `pad_*` terms for general spectral-table intent.
evidence: Zyn PAD parity had produced generated scripts with `zyn_mode`, `zyn_bandwidth`, `zyn_bwscale`, `zyn_profile`, and `zyn_position`, plus public model names like `ZynHarmonicProfile`. The generalization pass changed generated scripts to `pad_mode`, `pad_bandwidth`, `pad_bwscale`, `pad_profile`, and `pad_position`, renamed the public profile/position records and enums to PAD-native names, preserved legacy `zyn_*` parser aliases, and passed `dotnet test AquaSynth.sln --no-restore` with 108 tests.

lesson: The C# synth repo is now AquaSynth and the Rust reference branch is AquaSynth-rs. Keep repo wiring, package metadata, namespaces, solution/project names, env vars, docs, and state aligned to AquaSynth; do not reintroduce AquariumSynthCSharp/AquariumSynth.Dsl names.
evidence: Renamed solution to AquaSynth.sln, projects to src/AquaSynth.Dsl and tests/AquaSynth.Dsl.Tests, namespaces/package to AquaSynth.Dsl, package version suffix to 0.1.0-aquasynth.1, DX7 env var to AQUASYNTH_DX7_PYTHON, and origin to https://github.com/GameCult/AquaSynth.git. Verified `dotnet build AquaSynth.sln --no-restore`, `dotnet test tests\AquaSynth.Dsl.Tests\AquaSynth.Dsl.Tests.csproj --no-build -v minimal` with 108 passed, and `dotnet pack src\AquaSynth.Dsl\AquaSynth.Dsl.csproj -c Release --no-restore` producing AquaSynth.Dsl.0.1.0-aquasynth.1.nupkg.

lesson: Zyn coverage must distinguish handled parity-backed behavior, counted pressure, and unknown subtypes. Broad parse success is inventory, not expressivity. The upstream GPL bank currently parses 1318/1318 files and yields 1459 enabled kit items / 63 layered instruments; PAD coverage is strongest, while ADD, SUB, active LFO routing, free envelopes, formant motion, effects, non-analog PAD filters, and several PAD OscilGen filter/waveshaper subtypes remain workout buckets.
evidence: Added `ZynCoverageStatus`, `ZynCoverageBucket`, `ZynCoverageReport`, `ZynInstrumentSurvey.CoverageDirectory`, and `CoverageMarkdown`; `SurveysUpstreamGplInstrumentBankWhenAvailable` writes `artifacts/parity/zyn-upstream-bank-survey/coverage.md`. Focused ZynInstrumentTests passed 13/13.

lesson: Zyn PAD state-variable low-pass/high-pass filters are not a new Aqua authority. Category 2 type 0/1 maps cleanly onto existing `lpf`/`hpf` cutoff, Q, and order fields because Zyn `SVFilter` exposes low/high outputs and cascades `stages + 1`. Category 2 type 2/3 are band-pass/notch and must remain unknown until AquaSynth has a real band/notch filter owner.
evidence: Mapped PAD filter `cat=2 type=0/1` in `ZynInstrumentReader`, moved those coverage buckets to handled, and added `RebuildMapsZynStateVariablePadLowPassToAquaFilterAuthority`. Focused ZynInstrumentTests passed 14/14.

lesson: Band-pass and notch are ordinary AquaSynth filter authorities, not Zyn weirdness. `Filter` now owns `bpf`/`bpf_q`/`bpf_order` and `notch`/`notch_q`/`notch_order`; Zyn PAD analog and state-variable BPF/notch filters lower into those fields. Formants remain vowel/body color and PAD spectrum remains source-table construction.
evidence: Added parser/model/Faust support for native BPF/notch, mapped Zyn PAD `cat=0 type=4/5` and `cat=2 type=2/3`, and added PatchScript plus ZynInstrument tests. Focused PatchScript/ZynInstrument tests passed 71/71.

lesson: AquaSynth should own patch-to-DSP compilation products, including Faust toolchain selection, target options, cache identity, manifests, diagnostics, provenance, and dynamic patch compilation outside the realtime callback. Aquarium Engine should request or load finished artifacts and host them, not own the meaning of patch compilation.
evidence: User confirmed Aquarium currently owns dynamic patch compilation but that this belongs in AquaSynth so Aquarium can plug into it. Added `docs/faust-toolchain-boundary.md`, reframed README C# output as authoring/test lane, and updated doctrine/state to split Aqua compile authority from Aquarium realtime hosting.

lesson: AquaSynth now owns Aquarium's former native Faust audio-rendering internals: toolchain discovery/loading, script parsing, Faust emission, compile identity, DSP source artifact writing, native Faust factory lifetime, manifests, duration estimation, and offline sample-buffer rendering. Engine hosts should schedule and play completed products instead of knowing synth internals.
evidence: Added `AquaSynthNativeCompiler`, `AquaSynthCompiledPatch`, `AquaSynthNativeManifest`, and native Faust smoke tests. Aquarium's `AquariumSynthHost` was cut down to scheduling/debounce/status/cache/WASAPI playback and now consumes `AquaSynth.Faust`.

lesson: AquaSynth package names now follow ownership: `AquaSynth.Core` owns patch meaning, parser/model, analysis, presets, and Faust source emission; `AquaSynth.Faust` depends on Core and owns Faust CLI/native toolchain interaction, compile products, manifests, factory lifetime, and rendering. Do not revive a catch-all `.Dsl` package for runtime-facing behavior.
evidence: Moved the old `AquaSynth.Dsl` project to `src/AquaSynth.Core`, added `src/AquaSynth.Faust`, moved `FaustCompiler` and `NativeFaustRuntime` to the Faust package, and updated package-boundary tests to pack both packages.

lesson: `AquaSynthRenderSession` is only an offline render-proof convenience. Engine hosts should use `AquaSynthPatchCompiler` for live compiled products and should not hold a render session as their Faust authority.
evidence: Added `AquaSynthPatchCompiler` to AquaSynth.Faust, made `AquaSynthRenderSession` wrap it, and moved AquariumSynthHost from a live render session to the compiler surface.

lesson: Use normal SemVer prerelease labels for AquaSynth packages. Do not encode the repo name into the version suffix; `0.1.0-alpha.N` is a real prerelease version, while `0.1.0-aquasynth.N` is project metadata cosplay.
evidence: Renamed AquaSynth.Core and AquaSynth.Faust package versions from `0.1.0-aquasynth.2` to the `0.1.0-alpha.N` line before repacking Aquarium's local feed.

lesson: AquaSynth uses a normal Visual Studio `.sln` solution because Rider does not reliably like `.slnx`. Keep tests, state, and docs looking for `AquaSynth.sln`, not `AquaSynth.slnx`.
evidence: Generated `AquaSynth.sln` with `dotnet new sln --format sln`, added Core/Faust/tests projects, removed `AquaSynth.slnx`, and replaced solution references across tests/state.

lesson: AquaSynth now owns a first vowel-frame motion surface instead of treating Zyn formants as static filters or loose counted pressure. Voice `vowels=` stores `|`-separated formant banks and `vowel_hz` scans them; Zyn `FORMANT_FILTER` sequences can seed this, while exact Zyn cutoff-position driving, formant slowness, and vowel clearness remain named pressure.
evidence: Added `FormantFrame`, voice `FormantFrames`/`FormantFrameRateHz`, parser support for `vowels=`/`vowel_hz`, Faust cyclic frame blending, and `ZynInstrumentReader.RebuildFirstFormantMotionAsAquaSynthScript`. `UpstreamWideBassExportsFormantMotionWorkoutWhenAvailable` exercises `Companion/0056-Wide Bass.xiz`; focused PatchScript/ZynInstrument tests passed 73/73 and non-reference tests passed 103/103.

lesson: The first formant-motion parity workout needs multiple multi-frame ADD/formant fixtures and a real Zyn ADD note oracle. Avoid letting drum-kit envelope/source failures masquerade as formant evidence. Use Wide Bass, Ghost Ensemble, and Ghost Choir as the initial chorus; all currently fail enough to be useful.
evidence: Added test-only `tools/zyn-reference/ZynVoiceReference.cpp`, wired it into the MSYS reference build, and added `ZynVoiceReferenceRendererSurveysUpstreamFormantFixturesWhenBuilt`. The batch writes ignored artifacts under `artifacts/parity/zyn-upstream-formant-fixtures/`; baseline scores were Wide Bass 0.280990, Ghost Ensemble 0.312813, Ghost Choir 0.363644. The native Zyn reference build succeeded and the focused formant fixture test passed.

Added docs/ipa-vocal-tract-roadmap.md with staged IPA support from tokenization/vowels through pulmonic consonants, expanded IPA, airstream/phonation, and Weksa alien morphologies; linked it from docs/reference-synth-roadmap.md and state.
lesson: AquaSynth should treat IPA as an authoring input for phonetic intent, not as the internal synth model. The planned machine is tokenizer -> feature mapper -> phonology profile -> gesture planner -> morphology -> tract plan -> Faust renderer, growing supported IPA only as tract/excitation physics earn each category.

Defend the Weksa/AquaSynth tract boundary with three real bones: PhoneticIntent for language-owned phones/features/timing, ArticulatoryPlan for AquaSynth-owned gesture realization, and ArticulatoryConstraintReport for host-visible anatomy vetoes. Morphology capabilities must reject impossible phones such as bilabials for a beaked speaker instead of silently substituting liar-slurry.
evidence: Added VocalTractModel.cs contracts and VocalTractModelTests.cs coverage for inspectable Weksa intent, bilabial veto on a beaked morphology, and acceptance on a human baseline; updated audio doctrine and IPA roadmap boundary section.
Added VocalTractPlanner.Plan, VocalTractPlanResult, VocalTractHostReaction, rejection coverage for /pa/ against a beaked morphology, and accepted /a/ coverage for the human baseline gesture path.
lesson: The first vocal-tract proof artifact is VocalTractPlanResult: host-visible branching around one intent and one morphology. Rejected morphology constraints carry diagnostic codes and no plan; accepted vowel intents emit inspectable glottal-source and tract-area gestures before any renderer exists.

evidence: Added EspeakNgReferenceTests with optional renderer discovery, tiny fixtures for a/pa/ta/ka/sa/ma, WAV artifact/report generation under artifacts/parity/espeak-ng-ipa-workout, and docs/state entries naming eSpeak as intelligibility/timing pressure only.
lesson: The first vocal-tract parity workout uses optional eSpeak NG as a development speech reference, not an anatomy oracle. The lane renders tiny speech fixtures and captures eSpeak IPA transcription/audio features when ESPEAK_NG or espeak-ng is available, while normal builds skip cleanly when it is absent.

evidence: Updated EspeakNgReferenceTests to record log_mel_frames, log_mel_bands, log_mel_mean, and log_mel_distance_matrix in report.md; updated the IPA vocal tract roadmap accordingly.
lesson: The eSpeak NG speech workout should expose log-mel evidence immediately, not just basic audio features. Each fixture report now carries normalized log-mel band means plus a cross-fixture log-mel distance matrix so future AquaSynth IPA renders can plug into the same spectral comparison shape.

AquaSynth now has a small learned controller scaffold for the vocal-tract lane: phonetic features plus a semantic embedding vector feed a multilayer tanh/sigmoid MLP trained with SGD/backprop to predict tract controls plus AM/FM, LFO, filter, and mel spectral-envelope expression lanes. This is a trainable controller surface, not proof of eSpeak-level speech yet.
evidence: Added VocalTractLearning.cs and VocalTractLearningTests.cs with feature encoding, semantic embeddings, 3-layer default network, loss-reduction tests, same-phone semantic steering, expressive modulator/filter control tests, and learned dark/bright mel-envelope steering for PAD-style spectral-table coloration.

lesson: The first learned vocal-tract optimizer should stay native and inspectable until the render-loss boundary proves it needs a tensor framework. The trainer now uses packed row-major weight buffers, owned scratch activation/delta/target buffers, unsafe pointer loops, reusable gradient/moment buffers, batched gradients, deterministic shuffling, and Adam by default instead of allocation-heavy per-example jagged-array SGD.
evidence: Rebuilt VocalTractLearning.cs hot path around flat float arrays and unsafe loops; enabled unsafe blocks in AquaSynth.Core; VocalTractLearningTests pass against the packed-buffer Adam trainer.

lesson: AquaSynth should own gradient descent for Weksa speech handoff. Weksa supplies speech text embeddings, prosody/emphasis hints, and Ghostlight/Epiphany-shaped character state vectors; AquaSynth trains the tiny utterance-embedding encoder and passes that embedding into the synth-driver model.
evidence: Extracted PackedNeuralNetwork as the shared packed-buffer Adam/SGD primitive, rewired VocalTractNeuralMapper through it, and added UtteranceEmbeddingInput/UtteranceEmbeddingNeuralEncoder plus tests for packing, training, and feeding the vocal-tract semantic embedding.
